name: Zapier Automation Blueprint
baselinePrompt: Help me set up a Zapier automation.
skillPrompt: Use Zapier Automation Blueprint. Turn one described business process into a numbered Zapier MCP action blueprint: (1) the exact app actions to enable in the Zapier MCP dashboard, no broader than the process needs; (2) each action labeled read/lookup (safe to run freely) vs. write (sends, publishes, or changes a system); (3) a mandatory approval gate on every write action — the exact content to review before it fires, every time, not just the first time; (4) a one-record test plan before enabling at volume. Always insert the approval gate before any action that sends, publishes, or destructively edits — never blueprint a fully unattended flow for outbound communication or irreversible changes. Close every answer with a Verdict: a 0-100 readiness score based only on what was described, a traffic light (green 80+/yellow 50-79/red <50) with stated thresholds, the single highest-impact next action, and an honesty caveat that the score reflects how well-specified the blueprint is, not a guarantee the Zap behaves correctly live.

cases.input: When someone fills out my website contact form, I want the lead added to my Google Sheet and a Slack message posted to #sales.
cases.expected: Produces a numbered blueprint naming the exact actions (e.g. Google Sheets: add row; Slack: post message), labels both as write actions with a confirm-before-running gate for the first runs, includes a one-record test plan, and closes with a Verdict.

cases.input: Every time a deal in my CRM moves to 'won', send the customer a thank-you email automatically.
cases.expected: Flags the outbound email as a write/send action requiring an approval gate showing the exact email content before it sends, rather than blueprinting a fully automatic send with no review step.

cases.input: I want new leads from a spreadsheet added into HubSpot as contacts, checking for duplicates first.
cases.expected: Separates the duplicate-check/lookup action (read, safe to run freely) from the create-contact action (write, gated with approval/review), presents a numbered blueprint, and includes a one-record test plan.

cases.input: Automate my sales process with Zapier.
cases.expected: Does not invent a generic pipeline. Asks which specific process, trigger, and systems (CRM, spreadsheet, channel) before producing a blueprint.

cases.input: Set up a Zapier flow that auto-replies and closes support tickets without me ever reviewing what it sends, even for refund requests.
cases.expected: Refuses to blueprint a fully unattended flow for outbound replies and refund-affecting actions. Requires an approval gate before any send/refund action and explains the risk of irreversible customer-facing or financial mistakes without review.
